reason: The three roles (contract, provider, consumer) are the seam of the Go design: a contract package holding a Go interface and its typed service key, provider components that implement it, and model-facing tools that import only the contract, with an import-direction test that fails when a consumer imports a provider. That is decision DH-ADR-ARCH-6, and outcome DH-O-10 is the observable result.

The Go design keeps the three event domains and the boundary rule that a fact which must survive a restart is a session event (design.md section 4.6). DH-ADR-PERSISTENCE-1 makes the session log the single source of truth, and DH-ADR-ARCH-4 separates live events, declared as typed keys by their owner, from durable event types, which are registered.

The outcome is kept: a config value can change without restarting its component. The mechanism changes: a component that can take new config in place registers the port's update hook and receives the new typed config, so no schema volatility metadata and no shared reference is needed (DH-ADR-LOADER-7); a field is marked live with a tag that the harness schema package turns into a helper called inside that hook (DH-ADR-SCHEMA-5). The reference type itself is not built (DH-ADR-COSMOKIT-2, a recommended default the owner may overturn).

The rule is kept as requirement DH-LIB-ZOD-R13 of the schema specification: an optional argument that does not affect the requested operation is accepted, null decodes as absent, and every value that is used is still validated; test DH-T-ZOD-11 proves it. The first tool that applies it is str_replace_editor, whose null placeholders are treated as omitted (DH-D-FS-8). Which empty strings mean absent in grep, subagent and update_goal is each tool owner's declaration and is requested of areas A08, A12 and A13.

The Go port has the same shortcut in one accessor, Context.Root(). DH-ADR-TOOLCHAIN-8 makes an analyzer over callers of Context.Root() one of the required static checks from the first commit, so the rule holds without a baseline of recorded reads; upstream's baseline file is the debt unit that decision resolves.

Kept: a reload is not a transaction across entries, and an entry that fails to load is reported on its own while its siblings keep their new state (DH-D-LOADER-7; design.md section 5). Changed: what can be known before anything runs is checked first, so a static issue in an edit rejects the whole edit and the running tree is unchanged (DH-ADR-BOOT-7), where upstream applies sibling changes and leaves the bad entry on its old instance. What an operator sees after a half-applied reload is the per-entry report in loader.Reloaded (DH-D-LOADER-11).

DH-ADR-TOOLCHAIN-12 keeps the split: required CI jobs need no key, and scenarios that need credentials run in a separate workflow that is never triggered by pull_request_target. DH-ADR-TOOLCHAIN-6 keeps the second half: a scenario that was skipped or had no credential is reported as not run and is never a pass.

DH-ADR-TOOLCHAIN-14 keeps the gate: opening a session of more than 100,000 events is a budget test that runs the built binary in a fresh process and fails over a reviewed constant (its workload table names this note). The store's own measurement of the same path is M2 of the SQLite specification, test DH-T-SQLITE-8. The budget numbers are measured again for Go.

DH-ADR-TOOLCHAIN-14 keeps the three scenario groups (preparing each model request over a long history, another tool-heavy turn, discovering inactive fork children) as budget tests over one synthetic history; its workload table names this note. The tests themselves are written by area A02, which owns the path measured; that request is recorded for the integration of that area.

DH-ADR-TOOLCHAIN-14 keeps listing, content search and fork over a synthetic collection with the measured heavy-tailed size distribution, reused as test data; its workload table names this note. Listing and search latency over ten thousand sessions is measurement M4 of the SQLite specification, test DH-T-SQLITE-8.

DH-ADR-TOOLCHAIN-14 keeps the rerun: the heaviest budget tests run again in a Linux control group limited to 4 GiB and to 8 GiB of memory with no swap, in the scheduled workflow, and a case fails if it misses its budget or the kernel kills a process. The Go garbage collector reacts to a memory limit, so the rerun is as informative as upstream's.

The HTML report that scales each time to other hardware is not built. DH-ADR-TOOLCHAIN-14 replaces it: each budget test writes its measured time, peak memory and the runner's description to the run's artifact directory as a plain record, and the memory-limited rerun gives a measured number for a small machine where upstream's report gave an estimate.

Adopted from the start. DH-ADR-ARCH-3 makes every cancellable operation take a context.Context, derived from the turn, the agent and the owning fiber, with a typed cause; a seam contract is a Go interface (DH-ADR-ARCH-6), so the parameter is part of every capability method's signature and cannot be dropped between a tool and the work it starts. The fiber end of the chain is the lifetime context of DH-D-CORDIS-2.

Adopted as a framework guarantee and a component rule. DH-D-CORDIS-1 makes an unload wait for every cleanup in flight before it releases providers, so a provider's resources outlive the cleanup of every dependent (requirement DH-LIB-CORDIS-R5, test DH-T-CORDIS-2); the port also runs a fiber's cleanups one at a time in reverse order, which removes the concurrent-sibling cause. The order stop admitting, settle, drain, release is fixed for an agent by DH-ADR-AGENT-6, and each of the five upstream paths the note lists is a component whose owning area tests its own teardown.
